title: The Peril of Cymbaline Isle - Introduction - Who/What/When/Where/Why
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xm4ScqSNV10

Daniel (@dungeondive) sets out the philosophy behind his solo RPG series before a single die is rolled. The confession that drives it: what he remembers fondly from board games is almost never the system. It is the sense of adventure the components and art create, and the rules are frequently a hurdle rather than a pleasure.

So the plan is a set of boundaries rather than a box. *Scarlet Heroes* is the base ruleset, with *White Box* alongside it — both simple, both built for a lone hero. Everything else is drawn from the shelf: the *Dream Wars* map as an overland sandbox with some twenty portals to close, Luke Gearing's *Fever Swamp* for the marshes, *Vornheim* for cities, *Veins of the Earth* for caves, *The Dark of Hot Springs Island*, the *Dungeon Alphabet*, Table Fables, and Warhammer Quest for dungeon delves within the wider game.

He is candid about the risks — Scarlet Heroes' faux-Asian bestiary leaves him short of suitable standees, and he suspects he has bitten off more than he can chew. The best moment is a live demonstration: he shuffles the *Story Master's Tales* deck, draws the Shadow King and a swamp siren, and builds a possession-and-undead-uprising plot in about ten seconds.

----

Do you build solo games out of whatever is on your shelf, or does a campaign need one box with one set of rules to hold together?
